questions.prompt: What is a good test for whether a rule belongs in an Entity?

options.text: Whether the rule would still exist if this application were never built
Whether it is triggered by an HTTP request
Whether it formats data for the screen

questions.explanation: Entities hold enterprise business rules — general rules that would hold even without this app (on paper or in another system). App-specific orchestration belongs in use cases.

questions.prompt: Which things must a use case NOT know about? Select all that apply.

options.text: Who or what triggered it (web, CLI, job)
Where its data is stored (the database/ORM)
How its results are presented (the UI)

questions.explanation: A use case is ignorant of its caller, its storage, and its presentation. It DOES know the entities it orchestrates (an inward dependency).

questions.prompt: Another common name for a use case is an ______.
questions.explanation: A use case is implemented by an interactor, which orchestrates entities to fulfill one user goal.

questions.prompt: Match each rule to whether it's an Entity rule or a Use Case.

pairs.left: An order's total is the sum of its line items minus discounts
Placing an order: validate cart, reserve stock, charge, confirm
A coupon can't be applied twice to the same order
On checkout, email a receipt and enqueue fulfillment

questions.explanation: General rules that hold regardless of the app are entity rules; app-specific workflows that orchestrate them are use cases.

questions.prompt: Order these by level, from the innermost (most stable) outward.
questions.explanation: Stability decreases outward: entities change least, then use cases, then adapters, then frameworks.

questions.prompt: Why must entities be free of ORM/framework code?

options.text: It would make the innermost layer depend on an outer detail, violating the Dependency Rule
It would make the entities layer the outermost ring

questions.explanation: Putting an ORM/framework into an entity makes the most stable, innermost code depend on a volatile outer detail — the exact violation the architecture prevents.
